rules.title: An index repeats another one on the same columns, in the same order
rules.detail: This index has the same table, the same columns in the same order, the same method and no weaker a predicate than {duplicate_of}, so it is the same index under a second name. Both are maintained on every INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE, and both take cache that a useful index could use. Nothing in the schema says which one was meant to stay.
rules.fix: Drop one of them. If the two differ only in a WHERE clause, the redundant one is the partial index — the full one already serves those rows. If one of them backs a PRIMARY KEY or a UNIQUE constraint, that is the one to keep.

fires:
CREATE TABLE shop.events (id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY, at TIMESTAMPTZ);
CREATE INDEX idx_events_id ON shop.events (id);
silent:
CREATE TABLE shop.orders (id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY, paid_at TIMESTAMPTZ);
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_paid_at ON shop.orders (paid_at);
